primitives.name: Clearance Validation Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: `checkClearance()` (`apps/web/lib/scraping/clearance-engine.ts:85`) MUST run before every extraction job; a result with `allowed=false` stops the job.
primitives.assumptions: Each extraction job requires a valid clearance token before proceeding.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C = false, job execution halts immediately.

layer2.mapping: The clearance function maps to a logical predicate in GSE's state machine, where allowed = true corresponds to a valid transition.
layer2.telemetry: Job start time minus clearance check duration.

primitives.name: Freshness Constraint Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **CLAUDE.md rule 5 (no stale data)**: validate timestamps/freshness on every fetch; don't let a cached or delayed value pass as current.
primitives.assumptions: Data is considered stale if t_now - t_last > t_fresh.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If t_now - t_last > t_fresh, data is rejected.

layer2.mapping: Freshness check acts as a kernel in GSI's Bayesian update process, filtering out outdated evidence.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of records rejected due to freshness violation.

primitives.name: Provenance Guard Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Every extracted record MUST go through `wrapExtractedRecord()` (`clearance-engine.ts:367`), which throws if clearance wasn't granted.
primitives.assumptions: All records must carry verifiable provenance metadata.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If P(R) is invalid, wrapExtractedRecord() raises an exception.

layer2.mapping: Provenance guard mirrors GSE's integrity checks, ensuring all inputs are traceable and auditable.
layer2.telemetry: Number of records processed with valid provenance vs total.
